app.name: Decarbonisation Navigator
reg.title: Carbon regulations
reg.lede: Compliance cost year by year to 2050 under the EU ETS, FuelEU Maritime and the IMO Net-Zero Framework, plus the CII rating. Every parameter has a source and a check date.
scope.in_port: Within EU ports (at berth and movements)
scope.from_eu: Departures from the EU to third countries
scope.to_eu: Arrivals in the EU from third countries
ets.gases_hint: Split in the same way as CO2. They count in the ETS from 2026.
ets.chart.title: Annual EU ETS cost
ets.out_of_scope: With these details the ship is outside the EU ETS (category or tonnage).
ship.search.placeholder: IMO number, name (including past names) or company
ship.data_status: EU MRV · {ships} ships · {first}–{last} · latest release: {year} v{version} ({date})
ship.no_data.title: No EU MRV data imported yet.
ship.no_data.body: Download the yearly files from THETIS-MRV (mrv.emsa.europa.eu → Emission reports) into one folder and import it. Importing is done once and takes a few seconds; newer EMSA releases replace older ones.
ship.col.name: Name
ship.pick: Select a ship from the list.
ship.chart.title: CO2 EMISSIONS BY YEAR AND VOYAGE CATEGORY (t)
ship.mrv_note: EU MRV covers only voyages to, from and within the EU and time in EU ports. The ship's emissions on other voyages are not published.
import.title: Import EU MRV data
import.choose: Choose the folder with EMSA's .xlsx files
import.none: No .xlsx files found in the folder.
import.done: Imported {n} years. Skipped {skipped} (the same or a newer release is already present).
ets.from_mrv: Data from EU MRV: {name} (IMO {imo}), year {year}. Gross tonnage is not published; whether the ship falls under the ETS is taken from EMSA's figures.
ets.ratio: EMSA counts {pct} of the emissions the general rule gives for this ship (route exemptions such as islands). The ratio is applied until {until}; full coverage is assumed afterwards.
top.view.tip: EU: recorded EU MRV data only. WW: adds an estimate of activity outside the EU for the IMO rules.
in.domestic.more: The IMO Net-Zero Framework does not apply to ships on domestic voyages only. For EU MRV ships it is suggested automatically when every voyage is between EU ports and EMSA counts less than 20% of the emissions for the ETS (the pattern of an island service). Check it.
in.fuel.more.oil: Estimated from EU MRV data: the ship's CO2-to-fuel ratio ({cf} t/t) lies between heavy fuel oil (3.114) and marine gas oil (3.206), so the mix is split in proportion. EU MRV does not publish fuel types; change it if you know it.
in.fuel.more.lng: Estimated from EU MRV data: the CO2-to-fuel ratio ({cf} t/t) indicates LNG (2.750) with marine gas oil as second fuel. The engine type, which sets methane slip, is an assumption; change it if you know it.
in.eu_share: Share of activity in the EU (%)
ww.method.eu_dominant: Trades mainly in the EU: data taken as complete
ww.method.unknown: No estimate available; enter a value
ww.more: EU MRV records only voyages that touch an EU port; the IMO rules need total activity. Estimate: {hours} hours at sea in EU MRV ÷ days at sea of the class {cls} per the IMO study (most likely {days}, range {dlo}–{dhi}) = EU share {share} (range {low}–{high}). Check: the implied total fuel is {ratio}× the class average. The uncertainty analysis uses the whole range. If you know the actual share, enter it.
in.nzf.more: The adoption vote is scheduled for 4 December 2026. Targets and prices: MEPC 83 draft. Targets after 2035, prices after 2030 and the value of surplus units are not yet set; the assumptions used are marked in Parameters.
cii.need_capacity: The CII rating needs the CII ship type, capacity and distance. EU MRV does not publish capacity; enter it in the ship details.
cii.more: CII is computed with the operating profile of the reference year, held constant. Reduction factors to 2030 from IMO; after 2030 an assumption (+2.625 points a year). Ships rated E, or D for three consecutive years, need a corrective action plan.
step.ship.lede: Search the ships in EU MRV by IMO number, name (including past names) or company. Choose the ship to continue.
step.pos.lede: If the ship keeps operating as it does today, with the same fuel and routes, this is the carbon cost it faces to 2050. It is the baseline every investment is compared against.
pos.price.more: EUA allowance price paths (€/t) for 2025 · 2030 · 2050. Low: 70 · 80 · 100. Central: 75 · 110 · 150. High: 80 · 150 · 250. These are scenarios, not forecasts; the uncertainty analysis varies the price continuously. You can set your own values under Advanced.
pos.cii.need: Enter the ship's capacity for the CII rating:
pos.sentence: {ship}: operating as in {year}, its carbon cost rises from {a} in 2026 to {b} in 2035, reaching {total} in total by 2050.
pos.sentence.nzf: {ship}: operating as in {year}, its carbon cost rises from {a} in 2026 to {b} in 2035, reaching {total} in total by 2050. The IMO Net-Zero Framework accounts for {share} of the total.
pos.advanced: Advanced: all inputs and detailed results by regulation
step.3.lede: Every measure in the library is worked out on the ship's own power model: how much it cuts emissions, what it costs and whether it pays back. Tick the ones you want to compare in the next step.
step.4.q: What matters most to the company?
step.4.lede: Priorities are set with simple comparisons: which matters most, which least, and by how much. Each question shows how far apart your options really are, because that difference is what you are weighing.
step.5.q: Which option is best — and how sure is that?
step.5.lede: The options are ranked by four methods with your weights. The uncertainty analysis then checks how often the ranking holds when prices, measure results, the IMO vote and the weights themselves vary.
step.6.lede: A report ready for the board.
step.6.b1: • A PDF report with the decision, the data and the sources.
step.6.b2: • An Excel workbook with every calculation by year.
lobby.hero: Chart your ship's course to zero emissions.
lobby.lede: Find which decarbonisation investment suits each ship best under the EU ETS, FuelEU Maritime and the IMO Net-Zero Framework, and how certain that decision is.
lobby.new.title: New project
lobby.new.hint: Start from a ship in EU MRV.
lobby.data: Data: EU MRV (EMSA) · {ships} ships · {first}–{last} · release {last} v{version}
lobby.name: Project name
lobby.delete.confirm: Delete the project "{name}"? This cannot be undone.
lobby.import.error: The file could not be opened: {error}
std.pattern.more: The pattern sets how much of the activity is in the EU and how it splits: deep-sea 30% (mostly voyages to and from the EU), mixed 60%, mainly within the EU 100% (voyages between EU ports). Exact shares can be changed under Advanced in the next step.
std.note: 2018 class averages from the Fourth IMO GHG Study (2020). A specific ship's figures can be changed in the next step.
std.source: Standard ship: {name}, {size}, with averages from the Fourth IMO GHG Study.
pos.baseline.more: Comply at least cost: each year with a FuelEU deficit the ship takes the cheapest route for its whole carbon bill: the penalty, buying surplus from a pool (most likely {pool} €/t CO2e) or blending just enough biofuel (most likely {premium} $/t extra), which also lowers the ETS and IMO costs. Pay the penalties: the ship changes nothing and pays penalties that rise 10% for each consecutive year. Investments are compared with the first option.
pos.size.confirm: Typical size for the type: please confirm the actual size
pos.size.more: EU MRV does not publish capacity. Estimate: most likely {likely} {unit}, range {low}–{high} {unit}. Method: {method}. If you know the actual size, enter it; it replaces the estimate.
size.method.type: only the typical size range of the type in EU trade (IMO study, Table 92)
size.method.index+type: the ship's efficiency index (EEDI/EEXI) against the IMO reference line, combined with the type's typical range
size.method.hour+type: fuel per hour at sea (engine power) against the IMO study's class averages, combined with the type's typical range
size.method.index+hour+type: EEDI/EEXI index and fuel per hour, combined with the type's typical range
opt.start.more: The year the measure starts working. Retrofits are usually done at a scheduled dry-docking; days off-hire are costed at market daily earnings.
opt.life.more: How many more years the ship will operate (up to 2050). The IMO study assumes a 25-year life. A measure that outlives the ship keeps a residual value; one that wears out sooner is renewed.
opt.prices.more: Three price paths for every fuel to 2050, from DNV (2026), Lloyd's Register & UMAS (2020), EMSA and market prices in October 2026. Low = the lowest source value, high = the highest, central = the median.
opt.rate.more: The rate at which future savings and costs are brought to today's value (net present value). DNV (2026) and EMSA (2026) use 8%.
opt.sentence: {n} of the {total} measures fit {ship}. {paying} pay for themselves under these assumptions. Cheapest cut per tonne: {cheap}. Largest cut: {big} ({cut}).
opt.no_model: There is not enough data for the ship's power model (time at sea, distance or fuel).
opt.shortlist: Ticked for comparison: {n}. In the next step you set what matters most and the measures are ranked.
opt.d.verify: Some values rest on one source or on an assumption; to be checked.
pri.method.more: BWM (Rezaei 2015): pick the most and least important and compare only with those — fewer questions and more consistent answers. AHP (Saaty 1980): compare every pair. Both check how consistent the answers are.
pri.q.bo: How much more important is “{best}” than “{other}”?
pri.q.ow: How much more important is “{other}” than “{worst}”?
pri.hint.families: How far apart your options are in each family:
pri.need_shortlist: Tick at least one measure in step 3 to see how far apart the options are.
pri.cons.bad: The answers contradict each other (ratio {cr}, limit {limit}). Please look at the comparisons again.
pri.compare.more: Entropy and CRITIC derive weights only from how much the options differ, without the company's view. They are shown for comparison; the ranking uses your weights.
dec.need_shortlist: Tick measures in step 3 to rank them.
dec.agree: Agreement between methods (mean Spearman correlation): {rho}. Close to 1 = same order.
dec.sentence.all: With your priorities, “{best}” comes first by all four methods.
dec.sentence.some: With your priorities, “{best}” has the best overall position; first by {n} of the 4 methods.
dec.methods.more: SAW: weighted sum. TOPSIS: distance from the ideal and the worst. PROMETHEE II: how much each option beats the others pair by pair. VIKOR: a compromise that limits the largest shortfall. “Overall” ranks by the average position.
dec.odds.more: Chances of the three outcomes (adopted as drafted / delayed one year / not adopted): equal 1/3 each; “adoption likely” 60/20/20; “rejection likely” 20/20/60. These are assumptions, not forecasts.
dec.sure.more: Weights are sampled around yours (Dirichlet distribution). “Very” = small spread, “Not very” = wide, “Not at all” = every possible weighting equally, as in classic SMAA.
dec.draws.more: Each future draws fuel and allowance prices, the pool price, every measure's effect and cost, the EU share, the discount rate, the IMO vote and the weights. All options face the same futures.
dec.smaa.ready: Ready to run; takes a few seconds.
dec.smaa.stale: Settings changed; run again to update.
dec.smaa.sentence: Across {n} futures, “{best}” comes first in {first} of cases. With its own “central” weights it stays first in {conf} (confidence factor).
dec.central: What must matter for it to win
dec.smaa.more: SMAA-2 (Lahdelma & Salminen 2001). “Rank 1”: rank acceptability index b¹. “Expected rank”: average rank. “Confidence”: how often it wins when only the data vary, with its central weights. The last column shows the two heaviest criteria in the futures where the option wins.
dec.acc.more: Each circle shows the share of futures in which the option takes that rank (SMAA rank acceptability): the larger, the more often; the first column is how often it comes first. The expected rank is on the right. The recommendation is in red, doing nothing in grey.
dec.map.lede: Which option comes first for every split of weight between two criteria families; the other families share what is left in your proportions. The red dot is your weights, the grey cloud the weights SMAA tries.
dec.map.you: your weights; grey: the weights SMAA tries
dec.map.note: With your weights “{name}” wins. Of the weights SMAA tries around them, {share} fall in the same area.
dec.map.more: The map uses the options' most likely values and a weighted sum, as SMAA-2 does. If the red dot lies deep inside one area, the decision withstands changes in priorities; near a border, a small change alters the winner. Hover over the map for details.
dec.profiles.lede: How well each option does on each criterion: the worst of the shortlist at the centre, the best on the rim. The recommendation is in red.
dec.profiles.more: Values are normalised min–max within the shortlist, as in SAW; for criteria where less is better (cost, days, exposure) the scale is reversed. Hover over a spoke for the actual value. The shape's area is not a score: the score depends on the weights.
dec.radar.lede: Your weights (red) on a radar screen. The green echoes are weight sets SMAA tries around yours that keep the recommendation first; the amber ones are those for which another option wins.
dec.radar.more: Each spoke is a criterion and the distance from the centre its weight (the rings give the percentage). Where amber echoes reach beyond the green ones on a spoke, the decision is sensitive: if that criterion counted more or less, the first place would change. Computed with the most likely values and a weighted sum; hover over a spoke for the range.
dec.radar.note: In {share} of the weight sets around yours, “{best}” stays first.
dec.3d.lede: The same triangle in three dimensions: the height is the recommendation's lead over the next option. Above the “sea” the recommendation stays first; below it another option wins. Drag with the mouse to turn it.
dec.3d.more: Height = the recommendation's SAW score minus the best of the others, for every split of weight between the two families. The red buoy is your weights: the higher above the sea, the larger the margin. The surface colour shows which option wins at each point.
dec.fan.more: Each thin line is one SMAA future (the first 400 are drawn): the investment's cumulative discounted cash flow from today to the end of the horizon, compared with doing nothing. Where a line ends is that future's net present value. On the right, the distribution of the NPV over all futures; the shares count every future.
dec.fan.gain: of futures: the investment pays back (NPV > 0)
dec.fan.loss: of futures: it costs more than it saves
pos.donut.caption: How the {a}–{b} cost splits: {total}
